untranslatable_categories.reason: An application/problem+json document is answered to a caller that matches on its type and status, not to a visitor reading a page. Its title and detail are part of that machine contract, and a translated one would differ between two installations answering the same failure.
A stable machine error code is matched on by every caller. A translated error code is a broken contract.
An audit action name is a key in an evidence record, compared across installations and releases.
A log line is read by an operator through a log pipeline and by tooling that greps it, not by a visitor.
A developer exception exists for whoever is reading the stack trace. It never reaches a rendered page: the problem-details boundary answers a constant detail and logs the real message.
Contribution manifest text describes a route, listener or projection to whoever is reading the extension contract. It is developer-facing metadata about the surface, not the surface's own wording.
Reference specimen content in the interface-standard gallery exists to demonstrate a component, so it is deliberately fixed sample text rather than wording an operator reads as instruction.
Content a migration or a demo profile seeds becomes operator-owned content the moment it is installed, and content translation is its own model.
The MCP capability catalogue is consumed by a protocol client selecting a tool, not rendered to a person.
